title: AgentOS Distribution Alpha Task Plan
objective: Turn the completed runtime foundation into a distribution Alpha with packaged runtime artifacts, persistent state, runtime-aware image assembly, QEMU runtime smoke, release provenance, and first Alpha isolation workstreams.
assumptions: Runtime Foundation final audit has completed and is the mandatory prerequisite for Alpha work.
The Alpha base is Developer VM first and Cloud VM compatible.
The packaged runtime must remain runnable in stub/local-only ModelBroker mode.
The Alpha image path may start from the current initramfs machinery but must validate rootfs runtime artifacts before promotion.
Firecracker work belongs behind SecurityExecutionEngine and cannot bypass policy, capability, EffectEnvelope, audit, rollback, or recovery.
Generated build, boot, target, cache, and artifact outputs must not be committed.

waves.name: Alpha Scope and Packaging Contract
waves.purpose: Freeze the Distribution Alpha scope and create the install contracts that later image work must satisfy.
exit_criteria: Alpha scope depends on Runtime Foundation final audit and rejects MVP skeleton-only promotion.
Rootfs runtime artifact manifest lists every required runtime file, path, owner/mode expectation, and validation.
Runtime state directories for runs, audit, rollback, and memory have persistence and secret-safety contracts.
Policy pack, semantic tool manifest, and ModelBroker config have packageable defaults.

waves.name: Runtime-Aware Image Assembly
waves.purpose: Create an image/rootfs assembly path that installs runtime contracts before boot smoke promotion.
exit_criteria: A local validation command can reject missing or malformed Alpha runtime artifacts.
Image assembly records agentd, policy, tools, ModelBroker config, persistent directories, and release metadata in a manifest.
QEMU handoff remains compatible with the existing boot smoke path.

waves.name: Packaged Runtime Proofs
waves.purpose: Prove the packaged runtime still executes through AgentCore and Security Execution Foundation.
exit_criteria: Approved and denied service recovery smoke runs from packaged runtime artifacts.
QEMU boot smoke proves handoff plus runtime availability.
Release provenance records runtime gate commands, image inputs, and artifact hashes.

waves.name: Alpha Isolation Workstreams
waves.purpose: Add the first high-risk Alpha workstreams without creating a parallel side-effect path.
exit_criteria: Firecracker executor profile is represented behind SecurityExecutionEngine.
Package install isolation workflow uses policy, capability, audit, and rollback semantics.
Untrusted content workflow enforces source-to-sink policy and cannot directly drive high-risk tools.

waves.name: Alpha Promotion Audit
waves.purpose: Decide whether the Distribution Alpha image can be promoted or which risks block promotion.
exit_criteria: All planned Alpha gate commands have direct evidence.
Generated artifacts remain untracked or intentionally documented.
The workflow records either an Alpha promotion decision or explicit blocking risks.

confidence.notes: Plan is grounded in the Runtime Foundation Alpha entry contract, but exact rootfs/image implementation may change once the install manifest is written.
